title: Transactional Commit Queue with Rollback Support
concept: Two-Phase Commit & Rollback on Host Mutation Failures
problemStatement: Implement `createTransactionalReconciler()` that stages host mutations in a queue. If any mutation in the batch throws during commit, all previously executed mutations in that batch MUST be rolled back to their previous state.
interviewTrap: During Concurrent Mode, if React aborts a render, work-in-progress fibers are simply discarded without touching the host DOM. But once the commit phase starts, mutations must either succeed cleanly or trigger an error boundary.

testCases.name: Commits staged mutations successfully
testCases.testFn: let a = 0; const r = createTransactionalReconciler(); r.stage({ execute: () => a += 1, rollback: () => a -= 1 }); const res = r.commit(); return res.success && a === 1;

testCases.name: Rolls back previously executed mutations if an error occurs mid-commit
testCases.input: first op modifies val, second op throws -> val restored
testCases.testFn: let state = 0; const r = createTransactionalReconciler(); r.stage({ execute: () => state = 10, rollback: () => state = 0 }); r.stage({ execute: () => { throw new Error('DOM Error'); }, rollback: () => {} }); r.commit(); return state;

testCases.name: Clears staged operations queue after execution
testCases.input: re-committing empty queue succeeds with no extra operations
testCases.testFn: const r = createTransactionalReconciler(); r.stage({ execute: () => {}, rollback: () => {} }); r.commit(); return r.commit().success;

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does a Transactional Two-Phase Commit reconciler handle host mutation failures?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: A Transactional Reconciler records an 'undo log' (inverse mutation operations) during the commit phase. If a host mutation fails (e.g. out-of-memory or invalid host node state), the reconciler intercepts the exception in a `try...catch`, halts forward mutations, and replays the undo log in reverse order, rolling back all previously applied host mutations to leave the host tree in a clean, consistent prior state.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: High-level database/systems reliability question in custom renderer design.

realWorldUseCases.description: Controlling microcontrollers or industrial displays where hardware write failures must roll back to safe default states.

howToExplain.opening: A transactional reconciler brings database-style ACID rollbacks to React commit phases, maintaining an inverse mutation journal to restore host consistency if mutations fail.
keyPoints: Records inverse operations before executing host mutations.
Catches mutation errors during the commit phase.
Replays rollback log in reverse order to restore previous state.
Guarantees all-or-nothing host state integrity under failure.
howToExplain.closingImpression: Transactional commits prevent corrupt, partially-applied UI states in mission-critical hardware and financial renderers.
analogies: A bank wire transfer: if debiting Account A succeeds but crediting Account B fails, the system rolls back the debit so money is never lost.

commonMistakes.mistake: Replaying the rollback log in forward order.
commonMistakes.why: Rollbacks must execute in reverse order (LIFO) to properly unwind dependent tree mutations.
commonMistakes.correct: Iterate the rollback log in reverse order.

followUpDeepDive.question: How does React Fiber handle errors thrown during commitMutationEffects?
followUpDeepDive.answer: React wraps the commit phase in error handlers; if a mutation throws, React captures it, schedules an unmount of the failed root, and invokes Error Boundaries.
